pages.quiz:
ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. going
   C. went
   D. goed

3. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

4. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

5. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

6. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

7. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

8. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. where is the library
   C. Where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

9. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. run
   D. blue

10. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

11. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Spelling Antonyms, Synonyms and Numbers 12.5.1 Writing process-Dialogues 13.5.1  and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening: Views/ Opinions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening: Views/ Opinions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Trickster Narratives.

2. C — went

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Oral Narratives.

4. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

7. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

8. D — Where is the library?

9. C — run

10. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Conversational Skills: Polite Language.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Spelling Antonyms, Synonyms and Numbers 12.5.1 Writing process-Dialogues 13.5.1 ; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening: Views/ Opinions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening: Views/ Opinions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
